goal: Add a `control_commands` table and `enqueue_command`/`claim_commands` store verbs with claim-once semantics behind the store protocol across the sqlite/in-memory/postgres implementations, accompanied by a schema-version bump and a forward migration that upgrades existing stores cleanly.

relevant: src/flywheel/store_protocols.py — where the control-command verbs and record type register, alongside EventStore / SdkMessageStore
src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py — _next_run_sequence, schema version / migrations; add control_commands and bump the version
src/flywheel/store_memory.py — mirror the verbs and table in-memory
src/flywheel/store_postgres.py — mirror the verbs and table
src/flywheel/_schema/persistence-schema.sql — the SQLite schema and its Postgres mirror; add the control_commands table
references: src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py:_next_run_sequence — mirror the per-run sequence/atomic-claim pattern for claim-once
src/flywheel/store_protocols.py — mirror the EventStore / SdkMessageStore protocol surface for the new control-command verbs
constraints: claim_commands must be claim-once and atomic so a command applies a single time even with watcher restarts or concurrent workers.
enqueue_command(run_id, kind, payload) persists a pending command; claim_commands(run_id) returns and marks pending commands for that run exactly once, in enqueue order.
The migration bumps the schema version and forward-upgrades existing stores cleanly; no data loss.
Provide the verbs and table across all three implementations (sqlite, in-memory, postgres) and keep the SQLite schema and its Postgres mirror in sync.
Keep flywheel.task and flywheel.lifecycle purity untouched; control commands are execution-time telemetry, not domain events.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file touched and fix all Pylance errors in the same turn.
Commit with a Conventional Commits `feat:` message before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: No invoker watcher, CLI subcommands, or command application logic; this task is the store layer only.
No changes to graders or validation.
edge_cases: Claim twice: the second claim_commands call returns nothing for already-claimed commands.
Concurrent workers claiming the same run: only one claim wins per command; no double-claim.
Command enqueued for a run that is not in-flight: it is persisted as pending and never silently dropped.
Empty queue: claim_commands returns an empty result with no error.
Existing store without the table: the forward migration creates control_commands and bumps the version without losing prior data.
